name: Hulsa
body:
HULSA
CR 10

XP 9,600
CN Medium fey
Init +9; Senses low-light vision, see invisibility; Perception +31

DEFENSE

AC 24, touch 16, flat-footed 18 (+5 Dex, +1 dodge, +8 natural)
hp 127 (17d6+68)
Fort +9, Ref +15, Will +15
Defensive Abilities solar adaptation, void adaptation
DR 10/cold iron; Immune electricity, fire; Resist cold 10; SR 21

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., fly 60 ft. (perfect)
Melee solar weapon +14/+14 (1d10+1 S plus 3d6 fire, 19–20/×2)
Ranged light ray +13 touch (5d6 electricity & fire plus faerie fire [1d4 rounds])
Special Attacks kaleidoscopic glow
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 10th, concentration +13)

Constant—see invisibility
At will—life bubble

STATISTICS

Str 13 (+1); Dex 20 (+5); Con 18 (+4); Int 16 (+3); Wis 20 (+5); Cha 17 (+3)
Base Atk +8; CMB +9; CMD 34
Feats Combat Reflexes, Defensive Combat Training, Dodge, Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Point-Blank Shot, Skill Focus (Perception), Weapon Finesse, Weapon Focus (solar weapon)
Skills Acrobatics +25, Fly +33, Knowledge (arcana, engineering, planes) +20, Knowledge (geography, nature) +23, Perception +31, Sense Motive +25
Languages Common, Sylvan; electromagnetic communication
SQ life-giving glow, solar manifestation (solar weapon, improved manifestation), starflight, stellar alignment (photon), stellar revelations (soul furnace, supernova), zenith revelations (miniature star)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Electromagnetic Communication (Su)

A hulsa can communicate with other creatures within the same star system. With other hulsas and with creatures with the shortwave trait, this ability functions as telepathy. Otherwise, the hulsa mentally broadcasts to technological devices capable of receiving wireless signals, such as commset units.

Flashing Strikes (Ex)

When making a full attack entirely with melee weapons, a hulsa makes all iterative attacks at its full base attack bonus. Apply other penalties (such as for two-weapon fighting or for not being proficient with a weapon) normally.

Kaleidoscopic Glow (Su)

A hulsa is supernaturally luminous, shining bright light out to a range of 30 feet, normal light for another 30 feet, and dim light for another 30 feet. A magical effect can reduce the light in this area only if its source has a higher caster level than the hulsa’s CR. A hulsa can extinguish or relight their light as a move action.

In addition, 3 times per day as a standard action, the hulsa can oscillate the bright light from this ability for as long as the fey maintains concentration.

Creatures within 90 feet of the hulsa that can see this light become fascinated while the effect lasts and for 1 round after it ends (Will DC 21 negates). The hulsa can instead focus the glow on one creature, which works like charm monster with a maximum duration of 10 rounds (Will DC 21 negates).

Hulsas are immune to this ability. This is a mind-affecting effect, and the save DC is Charisma-based.

Life-Giving Glow (Su)

As a standard action, a hulsa can channel positive energy to heal living creatures within the area of their bright light. Determine the amount of damage healed and the number of uses per day as a cleric’s channel positive energy ability, using the hulsa’s Hit Dice as its effective cleric level (9d6, 6/day for the typical hulsa). Alternatively, the hulsa can use this ability to harm undead creatures in the area of effect (Will DC 21 half).

Light Ray (Su)

As a standard action, a hulsa can fire a light ray at a single target within 200 ft. as a ranged touch attack. Any creature taking damage from this attack is affected as if by faerie fire for 1d4 rounds.

Solar Adaptation (Ex)

A hulsa can survive without water, air, or food, living entirely on the energy provided by the stars. A hulsa can survive within a star despite the luminance, pressure, radiation, and convection currents. In addition, while within a star, the hulsa can move as if it had a supernatural fly speed equal to its fastest speed.

Starflight (Ex)

A hulsa can travel through the void of space at phenomenal speeds, roughly equal to a starship GTSG traveling at standard thruster speeds.

Stellar Alignment (Su)

A hulsa is aligned to the cycles of its solar systems, and gains certain abilities like a solarian of a level equal to its CR, as shown. A hulsa is always considered aligned to photon mode, but is not always fully aligned. After rolling initiative or using a zenith revelation, it can become fully aligned after 1d3 rounds have passed. Hulsas are never aligned to graviton mode and cannot gain graviton-related solarian abilities.

Void Adaptation (Ex)

A hulsa has immunity to cosmic rays and the environmental effects of vacuum, as well as the no breath universal monster ability. (A hulsa doesn’t breathe, and it is immune to effects that require breathing, such as inhaled poison.

This does not give it immunity to cloud or gas attacks that don’t require breathing.)

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, pair, or constellation (3–5)
Treasure standard

Although they look more like inevitables or golems, hulsas are actually fey. They appear to be constructed out of gleaming metallic armor plates that interlock in unusual ways.

Their faces look like domed helms almost completely lacking in expression, and ornamental wings adorn their backs. These wings often look more like clockwork cogs than bird wings, and while they may whirl and spin with flashing lights, they don’t operate in the way normal wings do.

Like ravais, hulsas are fey representatives of stars. Each hulsa is bound to a specific star and its planetary system, although they may travel far and wide throughout the Galaxy. While ravais represent the heat and light of stars, hulsas are more concerned with the celestial mechanics that govern the universe.

Hulsas are deeply attuned to these cosmic forces and cycles, and they often serve missions that are entirely indecipherable to others. Their actions may seem erratic, even bizarre, but they demand to be respected.

Any who interfere with a hulsa’s plans will be treated as threats to be eliminated, but those who cooperate could be rewarded.

While hulsas usually travel alone, some have even traveled with others whose objectives have aligned with their own, if only briefly.
